key_insight: Patient-aware sequence sampling can reduce bias in EHR pretraining and improve autoregressive foundation model performance compared with concatenating all patient records into a single stream.
clinical_relevance: For EHR-based AI systems, how training sequences are built may meaningfully affect downstream clinical prediction quality and fairness across patients with different record lengths.
method: Compared Patient Sampling against the standard Global Stream pretraining approach.
Used stochastic sampling with controllable weighting across patients.
Evaluated downstream performance on MIMIC-IV v2.2 and v3.1 clinical tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved Macro AUROC and AUPRC across downstream tasks on two MIMIC-IV versions when using Patient Sampling.
watch_item: Sequence-construction choices can change which patients contribute more training updates, so implementation must be careful to avoid new sampling biases or validation leakage.
paper_title: Pretraining EHR Foundation Models with Patient-Aware Sampling
